correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the ten icosahedral vertices after deleting a diametrically opposite pair and the 20 length-two edges. Five antipodal representative normals have nonzero triple determinants, so their great-circle arrangement on the sphere has exactly 22 open chambers. Independently enumerating integer plane normals in [-5,5]^3 produced 22 distinct strict sign vectors with crossed-edge support exactly 6 (ten chambers) and 10 (twelve chambers): combined with the rigorous chamber upper count this is exhaustive, not random evidence. A generic section has one polygon vertex per crossed edge, proving no 8-gon. Every equal edge subtends theta=acos(1/sqrt5); rotational invariance gives E[N]=20theta/pi, so Pr(N=10)=5theta/pi-3/2 and Pr(N=6)=5/2-5theta/pi, both positive. Measure-zero boundary normals excluded. The source Q(phi) verifier includes exact rational-enclosure signs and facet checks.
